summary.text: St. Noah is remembered for the ark, the flood and God’s covenant, and is named among the righteous Forefathers in the Orthodox calendar.

blocks.text: Genesis introduces St. Noah as a righteous man in a world marked by violence and corruption. God commands him to build an ark for his household and living creatures. His response is described as obedience to the command he receives.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The narrative recounts entry into the ark, the flood, the receding waters and Noah’s sending of birds to learn whether the land is dry. After leaving the ark he offers sacrifice. God gives a covenant concerning the earth and places the rainbow as its sign. Genesis also records a later episode of drunkenness, so the narrative is not a claim that every action of his life was faultless.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Genesis gives St. Noah’s lifespan as 950 years and records his death. The narrative does not describe martyrdom, and this profile does not convert its chronology into an independently established modern date.

blocks.text: The OCA commemorates St. Noah among the Forefathers and identifies the ark as a figure of the Church. A figure or type is an earlier event understood to anticipate a later saving reality.
